The '''1940–41 Národní liga''' (English: ''National league'') was the second season of the [[Czechoslovak First League|Národní liga]], the first tier of [[Football league system in Czechoslovakia|league football]] in the [[Nazi Germany]]-annexed [[Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia]] which had been part of [[Czechoslovakia]] until March 1939.

The Czech championship was won by [[Slavia Prague]],<ref name="List" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablest/tsjslchamp.html |title=Czechoslovakia - List of Champions |date= |website= Rsssf.com |publisher= |access-date= 27 January 2016}}</ref> and [[Josef Bican]] was the league's top scorer with 38 goals.<ref>{{cite book|first=Luboš|last=Jeřábek|title=Český a československý fotbal - lexikon osobností a klubů|publisher=Grada Publishing|language=Czech|year=2007|location=Prague, Czech Republic|isbn=978-80-247-1656-5|page=231}}</ref>

Czech clubs in what was now the German-annexed Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia continued their own league which was variously referred to as the Národní liga (English: ''National league''), Bohemia/Moravia championship or Česko-moravská liga (English: ''Bohemian-Moravian league'') while ethnic-German clubs played in the German [[Gauliga Sudetenland]].<ref name="List" /><ref name="Listczech">{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablest/tsjechamp.html |title=Czech Republic - List of Champions |date= |website=Rsssf.com |publisher= |access-date=27 January 2016 |url-status=live |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303215746/https://www.rsssf.com/tablest/tsjechamp.html |archivedate=3 March 2016 |df= }}</ref><ref name="Tables" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablest/tsjslhist.html |title=Czechoslovakia / Czech Republic - List of League Tables |date= |website= Rsssf.com |publisher= |access-date= 27 January 2016}}</ref>

In the [[Slovak Republic (1939–45)|Slovak Republic]] an independent Slovak league, the Slovenská liga, had been established in 1939 and played out its own championship which was won by [[ŠK Slovan Bratislava|ŠK Bratislava]] in the [[1940–41 Slovenská liga|1940–41 season]]. A national Czechoslovak championship was not played between 1939 and 1945.<ref name="Tables" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/slowchamp.html |title=Slovakia - List of Champions |date= |website= Rsssf.com |publisher= |access-date= 27 January 2016}}</ref>
